# Executive Summary

The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) establishes a harmonised European Union framework for managing digital operational resilience across the financial sector. It strengthens the ability of financial entities to withstand, respond to, and recover from ICT-related disruptions, cyber incidents, and third-party service failures.

This document provides a practical template for defining the organisation’s DORA governance model, ICT risk management approach, control structure, implementation roadmap, and assurance model. It can be used to document how the organisation aligns resilience, cybersecurity, third-party risk, and regulatory compliance into a coherent operating model.

# Overview

## Purpose

This document provides a practical template for defining, implementing, operating, and assuring compliance with DORA across the enterprise.

## Objectives

The main objectives of applying DORA are to:

-   strengthen digital operational resilience across regulated financial services
-   establish clear accountability for ICT risk and resilience
-   improve prevention, detection, response, and recovery capabilities
-   ensure consistent handling and reporting of ICT-related incidents
-   strengthen oversight of ICT third-party dependencies and concentration risk
-   support resilience testing and continuous improvement
-   integrate operational resilience with enterprise governance, risk, compliance, and assurance

## Scope

Describe the scope of DORA applicability in the organisation.

### In scope

-   regulated financial entities and relevant business functions
-   ICT services supporting critical or important functions
-   applications, infrastructure, cloud services, and networks
-   cyber resilience, ICT operations, and service continuity arrangements
-   ICT third-party service providers and contractual arrangements
-   digital operational resilience testing activities
-   incident management and regulatory reporting processes

### Out of scope

Document justified exclusions, if any.

## Intended Audience

-   Board and executive leadership
-   Chief Information Officer
-   Chief Information Security Officer
-   Chief Risk Officer
-   Operational resilience teams
-   Technology and operations teams
-   Procurement and vendor management teams
-   Legal and compliance teams
-   Internal audit and assurance teams
-   PMO / transformation teams

# Regulatory Foundation

## Background

DORA provides a unified regulatory framework for digital operational resilience in the financial sector. It addresses the management of ICT risk, resilience testing, ICT incident handling and reporting, ICT third-party risk, and supervisory oversight of critical ICT third-party providers.

## Regulatory Objectives

Document how the organisation interprets the regulatory objectives of DORA:

-   maintain resilience of ICT systems supporting business processes
-   reduce the impact of ICT-related disruptions and cyber threats
-   strengthen governance and accountability for ICT risk
-   improve visibility and management of third-party dependencies
-   increase consistency in resilience testing and incident reporting
-   enhance financial sector-wide resilience

## Core DORA Pillars

Describe how the organisation addresses the main DORA domains:

-   ICT risk management
-   ICT-related incident management, classification, and reporting
-   digital operational resilience testing
-   ICT third-party risk management
-   information-sharing arrangements

## Applicability and Entity Context

Document the specific applicability of DORA to the organisation, including:

-   legal entity structure
-   regulatory status
-   business model
-   group / subsidiary context
-   jurisdictional footprint
-   critical and important functions
-   supervisory relationships

# Governance Model

## Governance Objectives

Define the governance objectives for DORA compliance:

-   establish board-level oversight of digital operational resilience
-   define accountability for ICT risk and resilience decisions
-   align resilience priorities with enterprise risk appetite and business continuity objectives
-   embed DORA requirements into operations, architecture, procurement, and change
-   maintain evidence of compliance and control effectiveness
-   support continuous improvement through testing, monitoring, assurance, and remediation

## Governance Structure

Describe the governance bodies and their responsibilities.

### Example governance bodies

-   Board / Risk Committee
-   Executive Operational Resilience Committee
-   Technology and Security Steering Committee
-   ICT Risk Committee
-   Third-Party Risk Committee
-   Architecture Review Board
-   Incident Review Board
-   Internal Audit

## Three Lines Model

Describe responsibilities across the three lines.

### First line

-   ownership of business services, ICT operations, and controls
-   implementation of resilience, security, and continuity controls
-   incident handling and service restoration
-   evidence production and remediation execution

### Second line

-   ICT risk oversight
-   resilience policy and standards
-   compliance monitoring
-   independent challenge
-   regulatory coordination

### Third line

-   internal audit
-   independent assurance
-   control effectiveness review

## Sample Control Catalogue

| Control ID | Control Name | Objective | Control Owner | Frequency | Evidence |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| DORA-01 | ICT risk framework approved | Ensure governance and accountability | CIO / CRO | Annual | Approved framework |
| DORA-02 | Major incident process maintained | Ensure timely incident handling and escalation | CISO | Annual review | Incident procedure |
| DORA-03 | Testing programme executed | Validate resilience capabilities | Resilience Lead | Annual / quarterly | Test reports |
| DORA-04 | ICT third-party due diligence performed | Reduce supplier risk exposure | Third-Party Risk Manager | Onboarding / annual | Due diligence records |
| DORA-05 | Register of information maintained | Ensure complete supplier transparency | Vendor Management Lead | Ongoing | Register of information |
| DORA-06 | Recovery exercises completed | Validate restoration capability | Operations / Resilience Lead | Annual | Exercise evidence |

# Implementation Roadmap

## Maturity Phases

### Phase 1: Foundation

-   establish governance and accountability
-   define DORA policy framework
-   identify critical and important functions
-   establish asset and dependency baseline
-   define incident classification and reporting model

### Phase 2: Control Design

-   strengthen ICT risk management controls
-   implement resilience testing framework
-   formalise third-party governance and register of information
-   improve monitoring, response, and recovery controls

### Phase 3: Integration

-   integrate DORA with enterprise risk, architecture, and procurement
-   improve dependency mapping and concentration risk management
-   align service continuity, cyber resilience, and crisis management
-   automate evidence collection and reporting workflows

### Phase 4: Optimisation

-   mature dashboards and management information
-   strengthen scenario-based and threat-led exercises
-   improve remediation governance
-   enhance continuous monitoring and assurance

# Maturity Model

## Suggested Maturity Levels

### Level 1: Initial

Resilience practices are reactive, fragmented, and poorly evidenced.

### Level 2: Repeatable

Basic ICT risk, continuity, and incident processes exist but are inconsistently applied.

### Level 3: Defined

Policies, roles, testing, and third-party controls are documented and implemented across key areas.

### Level 4: Managed

Resilience capabilities are measured, risk-based, tested, and governed through regular reporting.

### Level 5: Optimised

Digital operational resilience is embedded across governance, architecture, operations, and supply chain management with strong assurance and continuous improvement.
